title: What If You Only Drank Sparkling Water?

scenes.text: What if you only drank sparkling water? Your teeth would be fine. The flavour is the problem.
The bubbles are carbon dioxide, which makes a weak acid. Plain sparkling water sits around pH five.
Sounds bad, but in lab tests it dissolved enamel about a hundred times less than soft drinks.
Within days you'd burp more, and some people get bloating. But it hydrates you just like still water.
And your bones? A big study linked cola to weaker hips in women. Other fizzy drinks showed no link.
The real danger is fruit flavour. Citric acid made some sparkling waters as erosive as orange juice.

description:
What if you only drank sparkling water? Plain sparkling water is mildly acidic, but a University of Birmingham study found it dissolved enamel around 100 times less than soft drinks, and it hydrates as well as still water.
Flavoured sparkling waters with citric acid were as erosive as orange juice in a 2007 study, and the Framingham bone link was found for cola, not other fizzy drinks.
